flawed_step: Step 4: passing from the verified necessary conditions (parity of the bipartition, 1-toughness of 3-connected cubic graphs, the bipartite component-excess condition) to the conclusion that a Hamiltonian cycle exists. No argument justifies this; the statement is exactly Tutte's 1971 conjecture, which is false.
counterexample: The Horton graph: 96 vertices, 144 edges, cubic, bipartite, girth 6, 3-connected, and non-Hamiltonian (J. D. Horton, 1976; reproduced in Bondy & Murty, Graph Theory with Applications, §9.6, as the disproof of Tutte's conjecture that every 3-connected cubic bipartite graph is Hamiltonian). Smaller published members of the same family: the Ellingham-Horton 54-vertex and 78-vertex graphs, and Georges' 50-vertex graph (smallest known). Structural mechanism, which I verified by hand: if a cubic graph is cut into fragments each joined to the rest by exactly 3 edges, then a Hamiltonian cycle must use an even number, hence exactly 2, of each fragment's 3 attachment edges (the cycle meets the fragment in vertex-disjoint paths covering it, and the number of used attachment edges equals twice the number of paths; 0 is impossible since other fragments exist), so the cycle crosses each fragment as a single Hamiltonian path between two attachment vertices and contracting the fragments gives a Hamiltonian cycle of the reduced cubic multigraph. Horton's fragments are bipartite pieces for which the required attachment-pair traversals are unavailable, forcing non-Hamiltonicity. Explicit checks I did carry out that show no cheap counterexample exists and hence why the witness must be large: (a) every 3-connected cubic graph is 1-tough, since each component of G-S sends at least 3 edges to S, giving 3c(G-S) <= 3|S| - 2i <= 3|S|, so no toughness-based witness is possible; (b) for S contained in one part Y of a cubic bipartite G, every component C of G-S satisfies x_C - y_C = e(C,S)/3 >= 1, so the bipartite alternation-excess obstruction is also vacuous. I did not re-derive non-Hamiltonicity of the 96-vertex graph by hand, and deliberately did not reproduce an adjacency list from memory; that part of the witness rests on the published construction.
assessment_summary: Attempted the proof in order. Steps 1-3 (bipartition parity; proof that every 3-connected cubic graph is 1-tough; proof that the bipartite component-excess condition is automatic for S inside one part) are justified but only eliminate obstructions. Step 4, the actual conclusion of Hamiltonicity, cannot be justified: the statement is Tutte's 1971 conjecture, disproved by Horton's 96-vertex 3-connected cubic bipartite non-Hamiltonian graph (only the planar restriction, Barnette's conjecture, remains open). Witness given as the Horton graph with the hand-verified 3-edge-attachment/parity lemma underlying such constructions and hand-verified proofs that toughness- and parity-based witnesses are impossible here; the non-Hamiltonicity of the 96-vertex graph itself is cited from the literature, not re-verified by hand, and this limitation is stated explicitly rather than papered over.
